subject.title: Model switch can fail silently when carried-over session context is too large

question: What should OpenClaw do when an existing session is switched to a model whose effective budget may not fit the carried context?
rationale: The code has metadata and pre-prompt compaction pieces, but choosing automatic compaction versus warning, fail-closed behavior, fallback routing, or a fresh-session handoff changes provider routing and session-state UX.

options.title: Warn and Offer Recovery
options.body: Keep model switching non-destructive, surface the target-budget risk, and offer `/compact` or `/new` recovery before the next run.

options.title: Auto-Compact on Switch
options.body: Attempt compaction during model switch when carried context exceeds the target budget, accepting extra latency and compaction side effects.

options.title: Fail Closed on Risk
options.body: Reject risky model switches until the user explicitly compacts or starts a fresh session, reducing silent failures but changing current permissive behavior.

recommendation.title: Warn and Offer Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep model switching non-destructive, surface the target-budget risk, and offer `/compact` or `/new` recovery before the next run.

likelyOwner.reason: The current model-switch and sessions.patch carrier lines blame to steipete, and this decision crosses core session/provider behavior rather than a narrow plugin boundary.
